speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing double vision, weakness in your upper limbs, and difficulty climbing stairs. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any trouble swallowing, slurred speech, or changes in your handwriting?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The double vision worsening with upward or downward gaze and weakness that fluctuates with activity are classic signs of a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, I need to check for specific muscle weakness patterns and assess your eye movements further.

REQUEST TEST: Edrophonium_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results from the Edrophonium test, pulmonary function, cervical MRI, and chest X-ray help rule out myasthenia gravis, respiratory failure, cervical myelopathy, and lung pathology. However, your specific complaint of diplopia worsening with upward or downward gaze combined with activity-induced proximal weakness strongly points towards a specific extraocular muscle and proximal muscle weakness pattern. Before we conclude, have you noticed any difficulty with chewing or speaking clearly, or do you experience drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of fevers, recent infections, and family history helps rule out systemic infections or hereditary neuromuscular conditions. Given your symmetrical proximal weakness and specific ocular diplopia that worsens with fatigue, have you noticed any ptosis or difficulty sustaining your gaze on one specific direction?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The gradual onset over a month, combined with symmetrical proximal weakness and diplopia worse with upward/downward gaze, is highly characteristic of a specific inflammatory myopathy. Have you noticed any muscle pain, stiffness, or difficulty rising from a seated position before standing?

REQUEST TEST: CK (Creatine_Kinase)
REQUEST TEST: Anti_Jo_1_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Creatine Kinase and negative Anti-Jo-1 antibody results are unexpected given your classic symptoms of diplopia worsening with upward/downward gaze and activity-induced proximal weakness. Does your diplopia improve significantly when you close your eyes or tilt your head?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The fluctuating nature of your weakness with clear improvement after rest is a hallmark sign that points toward a disorder of the neuromuscular junction, despite the initial normal Edrophonium test. I need to verify if this weakness affects your bulbar muscles specifically.

REQUEST TEST: Anticholinesterase_Test (Repeater_Dose)
REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
